full_judgment: 4. A bilateral lease deed between the petitioner and the Govt. was executed on 1.9.67 under heading "Long term lease of Khas land for non-agricultural purposes" initially for a period of 30 (Thirty) years from 1st September, 1967, with successive rights of renewal for a period of 30(Thirty) years in perpetuity for two further terms with full description of the land described in the schedule. A copy of the lease deed is annexed to the petition as annexure C. Thereafter, the petitioner took possession of the land as lessee and has been in possession of the entire land, falling with the boundary of plot leased out to him since 1.9.67 peacefully without any disturbance from any quarter. The petitioner, thereafter, submitted a plan for construction of a 3 storied building to the Municipality of Sylhet for approval. The said Municipality approved the plan for construction. The building as approved has been almost completed upto 3 storied, each floor containing 19 shop rooms which are let out to different persons on monthly rent basis. The petitioner, therefore, has possessed the entire area within the boundary described above. The land within the aforesaid boundary was more than 0.0577 acres or about 4 decimals of land by actual measurement, but in granting lease of the said land, the Govt. respondent did not retain any land as Khas of the Govt. as the possession of the entire land in Plot No. 7168 as described in the lease deed was given to the petitioner. Several suits were filed he different persons claiming title to the land and the petitioner as lessee of the Govt. was also made party. Title Suit No. 129 of 1965 was filed by one Kadir Hossain Khan impleading Province of East Pakistan which was dismissed. The petitioner filed Title Suit No. 97 of 1980 in the 1st court of Additional Sub-ordinate Judge, Sylhet agaisnt Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Sylhet, for declaration of his title confirmation of his possession and permanent injunction which was decreed. Copies of the judgment of the said suit is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure "E'. The petitioner's title being thus confirmed, he inducted tenant into the completed 3 storied building and there were as many 57 tenants in the petitioner's building. While in peaceful possession of the said building and land, the respondent No. 5 Mr. Ataur Rahman collusively created papers in his favour as licensee of 0.0019(8.-0X 10-0) in the said plot No. 7168 leased out to the petitioner. On the basis of Tahsilder's report submitted to the Upazila (Revenue) Officer, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, respondent No. 3, passed an order allowing lease of portion of the land in question on annual licence to respondent No. 5 subject to the condition that no pucca construction was to be made thereon and that lease would be cancelled without any notice as and when required for the interest of Republic. In passing the aforesaid order, the petitioner was not heard. This impugned order being Memo. No. SA/1361(2)/1(1) dated 4.4.84 was issued by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Sylhet, respondent No. 4, and is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure 'G'. Thereafter instead of implementation of the order for Eksona Licence, an agreement for licence to shop keepers in Govt. hats as per schedule 5 of the Govt. Estate Mannual was executed on 10.3.86 allowing the respondent No. 5 to construct building thereon which was signed on behalf of the Govt. by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer and respondent No. 5 on behalf of himself as licensee. A copy of the said licence deed impugned is Annexure to the petition and marked as annexure "H."
